docs.title: Analysis of Drag-and-Drop Text (Lückentext) Questions in Moodle XML Backups
docs.text:
Warning

The insights described on this page originate from reverse engineering conducted before the activity was implemented in Course as Code. Since small errors often came to light during the implementation process, and these were (unfortunately) not always corrected accordingly in the reverse engineering documentation, it's possible that the following information is in some parts incomplete or incorrect.

It is therefore recommended to always cross-reference the information with the implementation in the writer classes.

docs.title: General Information
docs.text: Drag-and-drop text questions (often referred to as "Lückentext" in German) are a question type in Moodle that allows students to fill in gaps in text by dragging and dropping words or phrases. These questions are represented as "ddwtos" (drag-and-drop words into text) in Moodle's question system. This document analyzes the XML structure used in Moodle backup files for drag-and-drop text questions.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text:
• Question Type: ddwtos - The question type identifier in Moodle
  • UI Presentation: Text with gaps marked by placeholders ([[1]], [[2]], etc.) that students fill by dragging words/phrases from a selection area
  • Drag Groups: Words/phrases can be organized into different groups (often color-coded in the UI)
  • Grading: Usually all-or-nothing or partial credit per correct placement

docs.title: questions.xml
docs.text: The questions.xml file contains the main structure and configuration of drag-and-drop text questions.

docs.title: Drag-and-Drop Text Question Base Structure
docs.text:
• Question ID: Unique identifier for the question (e.g., 14, 15)
  • Name: Name of the question (e.g., Computer Science Basics Q1, Linux File Permissions Q1)
  • Question Text: The text containing placeholders where words will be dragged (e.g., The [[1]] is a type of system software that manages [[5]] and software resources...)
  • Question Text Format: Format of the question text (typically 1 for HTML or 4 for Markdown)
  • General Feedback: Feedback provided to all students after attempting the question
  • General Feedback Format: Format of the general feedback
  • Default Mark: Default point value for the question (e.g., 1.0000000)
  • Penalty: Penalty for each incorrect attempt (e.g., 0.2500000)
  • Question Type: Specified as ddwtos
  • Length: Always 1 for drag-and-drop text questions
  • Stamp: A unique identifier with format [server-ip]:[port]+[timestamp]+[uuid]
  • Time Created: Unix timestamp when the question was created
  • Time Modified: Unix timestamp when the question was last modified

docs.title: Drag-and-Drop Text Specific Elements
docs.text:
The drag-and-drop text specific elements are contained within the plugin_qtype_ddwtos_question tag, which includes two main sections:

  1. answers: Contains the draggable text items (choices)
  2. ddwtos: Contains configuration options for the question

docs.title: answers
docs.text:
The answers section contains multiple answer elements, each with an id attribute. Each answer element includes:

  • answertext: The text of the draggable item (e.g., Operating System, Hardware)
  • answerformat: Format of the answer text (typically 1 for HTML)
  • fraction: Always 0.0000000 for drag-and-drop questions (not used for grading)
  • feedback: Contains serialized PHP object with drag group information:
  • Format: O:8:"stdClass":2:{s:9:"draggroup";s:1:"1";s:8:"infinite";b:0;}
  • draggroup: The group to which this draggable item belongs (e.g., "1", "2")
  • infinite: Whether the item can be used multiple times (b:0 for false, b:1 for true)
  • feedbackformat: Always 0 for drag-and-drop questions

docs.title: ddwtos
docs.text:
The ddwtos section contains an element with an id attribute and includes settings for the drag-and-drop question:

  • shuffleanswers: Whether to shuffle the draggable items (1 for yes, 0 for no)
  • correctfeedback: Feedback shown for a completely correct answer
  • correctfeedbackformat: Format of the correct feedback
  • partiallycorrectfeedback: Feedback shown for partially correct answers
  • partiallycorrectfeedbackformat: Format of the partially correct feedback
  • incorrectfeedback: Feedback shown for completely incorrect answers
  • incorrectfeedbackformat: Format of the incorrect feedback
  • shownumcorrect: Whether to show the number of correct answers (0 for no, 1 for yes)

In this example:

  • The question text contains two placeholders: [[1]] and [[5]]
  • There are 7 draggable items divided into 2 groups:
    • Group 1: "Operating System", "Compiler", "Microsoft Word", "Printer"
    • Group 2: "Hardware", "Internet", "Printing"
  • Shuffleanswers is enabled, so the draggable items will be displayed in random order

docs.title: Placeholder Syntax
docs.text:
The placeholders in the question text follow a specific format: double square brackets containing the number of the gap, e.g., [[1]], [[2]], etc. These numbers correspond to the positions where students should drag and drop the text items.

For example, in the question text: 

The [[1]] is a type of system software that manages [[5]] and software resources...

Students would need to drag:

  • The appropriate term to gap [[1]] (likely "Operating System")
  • The appropriate term to gap [[5]] (likely "Hardware")

The numbers inside the placeholders do not necessarily need to be sequential. They can be any integer values, but they should be unique within the question.

docs.title: Drag Groups
docs.text:
Draggable items are organized into groups, which is represented in the feedback element as a serialized PHP object. This serialized object contains two pieces of information:

  1. draggroup: A string value indicating the group number (e.g., "1", "2")
  2. infinite: A boolean value indicating if the item can be used multiple times (b:0 for false, b:1 for true)

The serialized format looks like: 

O:8:"stdClass":2:{s:9:"draggroup";s:1:"1";s:8:"infinite";b:0;}

In the Moodle UI, different drag groups are typically displayed with different background colors to help students distinguish them.

docs.title: Handling Categories in the Model
docs.text:
In the internal model, drag-and-drop text items often include a "Category" property that maps to the drag group in the XML. The mapping is as follows:

  • If Category is "A", it maps to draggroup "1"
  • If Category is "B", it maps to draggroup "2"
  • If Category is "C", it maps to draggroup "3"
  • And so on...

If Category is null or empty, it typically defaults to draggroup "1".

docs.title: Hints Implementation
docs.text:
The question_hints element can contain multiple question_hint elements, each with:

  • hint: The text of the hint
  • hintformat: Format of the hint text
  • shownumcorrect: Whether to show the number of correct answers after applying the hint
  • clearwrong: Whether to clear incorrect responses when the hint is shown
  • options: Additional options (typically $@NULL@$)

When hints are present, they influence the behavior of the drag-and-drop question in interactive or adaptive question behavior modes.

docs.title: Model-to-XML Mappings
docs.text:
When implementing drag-and-drop text questions in the internal model, the following mappings apply:

  1. DragAndDropTextQuestion model class maps to the question element with qtype="ddwtos"
  2. TextChoice model class items map to the answer elements
  3. The Category property in TextChoice maps to the draggroup value in the serialized PHP object in the feedback element
  4. Feedback settings map to corresponding elements in the ddwtos section
  5. Hint model class items map to question_hint elements

docs.title: Common Issues and Solutions
docs.text:
1. Serialized PHP Object: The feedback element contains a serialized PHP object, which must be properly formatted for Moodle to interpret it correctly.

  2. Multiple Drag Groups: When implementing multiple drag groups, ensure that:

  3. Each draggable item is assigned to the correct group
  4. The serialized PHP object in the feedback element correctly reflects the group assignment

  5. The question text contains placeholders that match the expected patterns

  6. Shuffle Answers: The shuffleanswers option determines whether the draggable items are displayed in random order (1) or in the order they appear in the XML (0).

  7. Placeholder IDs: The numbers inside the placeholders ([[1]], [[2]], etc.) should be unique within the question, but they do not necessarily need to correspond to the IDs of the draggable items.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Drag-and-drop text (Lückentext) questions in Moodle provide a way for students to fill in missing words or phrases in a text by dragging items from a selection area. The XML structure:

  • Uses the ddwtos question type
  • Defines draggable items with their text and group assignments
  • Uses placeholders in the question text to indicate where items should be dragged
  • Supports organizing draggable items into different groups
  • Allows for feedback at various correctness levels
  • Supports hints to guide students toward correct answers

When implementing a drag-and-drop text question writer or reader, special attention should be paid to:

  1. The format of the placeholders in the question text
  2. The correct generation of the serialized PHP object for drag group assignments
  3. The mapping between internal model categories and XML drag groups
  4. The handling of shuffleanswers and other configuration options

docs.title: Analysis of Dropdown (Matching) Questions in Moodle XML Backups
docs.text:
Warning

The insights described on this page originate from reverse engineering conducted before the activity was implemented in Course as Code. Since small errors often came to light during the implementation process, and these were (unfortunately) not always corrected accordingly in the reverse engineering documentation, it's possible that the following information is in some parts incomplete or incorrect.

It is therefore recommended to always cross-reference the information with the implementation in the writer classes.

docs.title: General Information
docs.text: In Moodle, dropdown questions are implemented as a type of "matching" question. These questions allow instructors to create prompts (sub-questions) where students must select the correct answer from a dropdown menu of options. This document analyzes the XML structure used in Moodle backup files for dropdown/matching questions.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text:
• Question Type: match - The question type identifier in Moodle
  • UI Presentation: Presents as a list of sub-questions, each with its own dropdown menu containing possible answers
  • Grading: Each sub-question is typically worth an equal portion of the total question mark
  • Answer Pool: All correct answers and distractors are pooled together to create the dropdown options

docs.title: questions.xml
docs.text: The questions.xml file contains the main structure and configuration of dropdown/matching questions.

docs.title: Dropdown/Matching Question Base Structure
docs.text:
• Question ID: Unique identifier for the question (e.g., 12, 13)
  • Name: Name of the question (e.g., Democracies around the world, Programming Paradigms)
  • Question Text: The instructions for the matching task
  • Question Text Format: Format of the question text (typically 1 for HTML)
  • General Feedback: Feedback provided to all students after attempting the question
  • General Feedback Format: Format of the general feedback
  • Default Mark: Default point value for the question (e.g., 1.0000000)
  • Penalty: Penalty for each incorrect attempt (e.g., 0.3333333)
  • Question Type: Specified as match
  • Length: Always 1 for matching questions
  • Stamp: A unique identifier with format [server-ip]:[port]+[timestamp]+[uuid]
  • Time Created: Unix timestamp when the question was created
  • Time Modified: Unix timestamp when the question was last modified

docs.title: Dropdown/Matching-Specific Elements
docs.text:
The dropdown/matching-specific elements are contained within the plugin_qtype_match_question tag, which includes two main sections:

  1. matchoptions: Contains configuration options for the matching question
  2. matches: Contains all sub-questions and their corresponding correct answers, as well as distractor options

docs.title: matchoptions
docs.text:
The matchoptions section contains an element with an id attribute and includes settings for the matching question:

  • shuffleanswers: Whether to shuffle the answer options (1 for yes, which is typical for dropdown questions)
  • correctfeedback: Feedback shown for a completely correct answer
  • correctfeedbackformat: Format of the correct feedback
  • partiallycorrectfeedback: Feedback shown for partially correct answers
  • partiallycorrectfeedbackformat: Format of the partially correct feedback
  • incorrectfeedback: Feedback shown for completely incorrect answers
  • incorrectfeedbackformat: Format of the incorrect feedback
  • shownumcorrect: Whether to show the number of correct answers (0 for no, 1 for yes)

docs.title: matches
docs.text:
The matches section contains multiple match elements, each with an id attribute. There are two types of matches:

  1. Sub-question matches: These have both questiontext and answertext elements, where:

    • questiontext: The prompt or stem for the sub-question
    • questiontextformat: Format of the sub-question text
    • answertext: The correct answer for this sub-question

  2. Distractor-only matches: These have an empty questiontext and only contain an answertext element:

    • questiontext: Empty (represented as "")
    • questiontextformat: Format (still present but irrelevant)
    • answertext: A distractor option that will appear in dropdown menus but isn't the correct answer for any sub-question

docs.title: Example Dropdown/Matching Question
docs.text:
Here's a simplified representation of a dropdown/matching question:

<question id="13">
  <parent>0</parent>
  <name>Programming Paradigms</name>
  <questiontext><p>Select the primary programming paradigm associated with each language.</p></questiontext>
  <questiontextformat>1</questiontextformat>
  <generalfeedback></generalfeedback>
  <generalfeedbackformat>2</generalfeedbackformat>
  <defaultmark>1.0000000</defaultmark>
  <penalty>0.2500000</penalty>
  <qtype>match</qtype>
  <length>1</length>
  <stamp>172.21.0.3:8080+1746965782+d76ee80668b945dd9fff588a80830952</stamp>
  <timecreated>1746958582</timecreated>
  <timemodified>1746958582</timemodified>
  <createdby>0</createdby>
  <modifiedby>0</modifiedby>
  <plugin_qtype_match_question>
    <matchoptions id="23">
      <shuffleanswers>1</shuffleanswers>
      <correctfeedback></correctfeedback>
      <correctfeedbackformat>2</correctfeedbackformat>
      <partiallycorrectfeedback></partiallycorrectfeedback>
      <partiallycorrectfeedbackformat>2</partiallycorrectfeedbackformat>
      <incorrectfeedback></incorrectfeedback>
      <incorrectfeedbackformat>2</incorrectfeedbackformat>
      <shownumcorrect>0</shownumcorrect>
    </matchoptions>
    <matches>
      <!-- Sub-question matches (prompt + correct answer) -->
      <match id="24">
        <questiontext><p>Haskell</p></questiontext>
        <questiontextformat>1</questiontextformat>
        <answertext>Functional</answertext>
      </match>
      <match id="25">
        <questiontext><p>Java</p></questiontext>
        <questiontextformat>1</questiontextformat>
        <answertext>Object-Oriented</answertext>
      </match>
      <match id="26">
        <questiontext><p>C</p></questiontext>
        <questiontextformat>1</questiontextformat>
        <answertext>Procedural</answertext>
      </match>
      <match id="27">
        <questiontext><p>Prolog</p></questiontext>
        <questiontextformat>1</questiontextformat>
        <answertext>Logic Programming</answertext>
      </match>

      <!-- Distractor-only matches (empty questiontext) -->
      <match id="28">
        <questiontext></questiontext>
        <questiontextformat>1</questiontextformat>
        <answertext>Functional</answertext>
      </match>
      <match id="29">
        <questiontext></questiontext>
        <questiontextformat>1</questiontextformat>
        <answertext>Markdown Language</answertext>
      </match>
    </matches>
  </plugin_qtype_match_question>
  <plugin_qbank_comment_question>
    <comments />
  </plugin_qbank_comment_question>
  <plugin_qbank_customfields_question>
    <customfields />
  </plugin_qbank_customfields_question>
  <question_hints />
  <tags />
</question>

In this example:

  • There are 4 sub-questions (Haskell, Java, C, and Prolog) with their correct answers
  • There are 2 distractors (one is a duplicate "Functional" which may confuse students, and "Markdown Language")
  • All these answers will be pooled together and presented in dropdown menus for each sub-question

docs.title: Answer Pooling
docs.text:
All answers (both correct answers and distractors) are pooled together to create the dropdown options for each sub-question. The XML structure represents this by:

  1. Including matches with both questiontext and answertext for sub-questions with their correct answers
  2. Including additional matches with empty questiontext and only answertext for distractors

docs.title: Duplicate Answers
docs.text: Note that in the example, "Functional" appears twice - once as the correct answer for "Haskell" and once as a separate distractor. In the Moodle UI, it will only appear once in the dropdown options, as Moodle automatically de-duplicates the answer pool.

docs.title: Wrong Answers List in Internal Model
docs.text:
In the internal model, dropdown sub-questions might include a "WrongAnswers" list property for each sub-question. When converting to XML, these wrong answers (distractors) become separate match elements with empty questiontext.

For example, a model structure like: 

new DropdownSubQuestion
{
    QuestionText = "<p>Java</p>",
    QuestionTextFormat = FormattingFormat.HTML,
    CorrectAnswer = "Object-Oriented",
    WrongAnswers = new List<string> { "Functional" }
}

Would be converted to:

  1. A match with "Java" as the questiontext and "Object-Oriented" as the answertext
  2. A distractor match with empty questiontext and "Functional" as the answertext

docs.title: Hints Implementation
docs.text:
The question_hints element can contain multiple question_hint elements, each with:

  • hint: The text of the hint
  • hintformat: Format of the hint text
  • shownumcorrect: Whether to show the number of correct answers after applying the hint
  • clearwrong: Whether to clear incorrect responses when the hint is shown
  • options: Additional options (typically $@NULL@$)

When hints are present, they influence the behavior of the dropdown question in interactive or adaptive question behavior modes.

docs.title: Model-to-XML Mappings
docs.text:
When implementing dropdown/matching questions in the internal model, the following mappings apply:

  1. DropdownQuestion model class maps to the question element with qtype="match"
  2. DropdownSubQuestion model class items map to the match elements with non-empty questiontext
  3. The WrongAnswers lists from sub-questions map to match elements with empty questiontext
  4. Feedback settings map to corresponding elements in the matchoptions section
  5. Hint model class items map to question_hint elements

docs.title: Common Issues and Solutions
docs.text:
1. Duplicate Answers: Be aware that Moodle de-duplicates the answer pool. If the same answer appears multiple times (either as correct answers or distractors), it will only appear once in the dropdown options.

  2. Empty Feedback: When feedback is not provided, the XML elements for feedback will still be present but empty.

  3. Answer Shuffling: By default, the shuffleanswers option is set to 1, which means the order of answers in dropdown menus will be randomized. This can be turned off by setting it to 0, but this is unusual for dropdown questions.

  4. Sub-question Formatting: Each sub-question can have its own text format, allowing for rich formatting using HTML.

docs.text:
Dropdown (matching) questions in Moodle provide a way to assess students' ability to match items from one list with items from another. The XML structure:

  • Uses the match question type
  • Creates an answer pool from correct answers and distractors
  • Presents sub-questions with dropdown menus containing all possible answers
  • Supports rich text formatting for question text and sub-questions
  • Allows for feedback at various correctness levels
  • Supports hints to guide students toward correct answers

When implementing a dropdown question writer or reader, special attention should be paid to the way the answer pool is constructed, ensuring that all correct answers and distractors are properly included in the resulting XML structure.

docs.title: Setting up a local Moodle Environment
docs.text:
First, we need a local Moodle instance that you can use to test and preview your exported courses. We use Docker for this with an image from Bitnami [hub.docker.com].

To set up a local installation of Moodle for development, follow these instructions:

  1. Create a new file: docker-compose.yml
  2. Add the following content to the file: 
    # Copyright Broadcom, Inc. All Rights Reserved.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: APACHE-2.0

services:
  mariadb:
    image: docker.io/bitnamilegacy/mariadb:latest
    environment:
      # ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD is recommended only for development.
      - ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes
      - MARIADB_USER=bn_moodle
      - MARIADB_DATABASE=bitnami_moodle
      - MARIADB_CHARACTER_SET=utf8mb4
      - MARIADB_COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
    volumes:
      - 'mariadb_data:/bitnami/mariadb'
  moodle:
    image: docker.io/bitnamilegacy/moodle:5.0
    ports:
      - '80:8080'
      - '443:8443'
    environment:
      - MOODLE_DATABASE_HOST=mariadb
      - MOODLE_DATABASE_PORT_NUMBER=3306
      - MOODLE_DATABASE_USER=bn_moodle
      - MOODLE_DATABASE_NAME=bitnami_moodle
      # ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD is recommended only for development.
      - ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD=yes
    volumes:
      - 'moodle_data:/bitnami/moodle'
      - 'moodledata_data:/bitnami/moodledata'
    depends_on:
      - mariadb

volumes:
  mariadb_data:
    driver: local
  moodle_data:
    driver: local
  moodledata_data:
    driver: local
  3. Start the containers: 
    (sudo) docker compose up -d
  4. Moodle is now reachable at http://localhost
  5. Log in with the default credentials: 
    user: user
password: bitnami
  6. Go to Site Administration > Courses > Backups > Asynchronous backup/restore and disable Enable asynchronous backups.
  7. Go to Site Administration > Plugins > Install plugins and install the CodeRunner plugin.
